requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject, any contributed source, or an acknowledgment supplied
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`. I did not read implementation source. All the tests are marked with `{test}` references to the subject.

**1. Direct references from the subject, a contributed source, or an acknowledgment must contribute the complete fenced declaration, including the phrase option.**
- **Subject:** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` has the subject `requirements.ready` reference `terms.unit`. It asserts that exactly two definition inputs are supplied.
- **Contributed source:** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_inputs_can_read_untracked_declarations_and_terms]` makes the `{test}` source in `src/lib.rs` carry a `{term}` reference to `terms.ready`. It asserts that the `terms.ready` definition input appears in `mandatory_inputs()`.
- **Acknowledgment:** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[acknowledgment_only_terms_are_supplied_and_validated_without_implementation_reads]` has a `{fixme}` body that references `terms.boundary`.
  - The prompt contains both "at the limit." and "A unit.".
  - It does not contain the implementation body.
  - No outline input is created for the acknowledgment's containing source.
- **Completeness:** `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[declaration_text_reaches_the_model_redacted]` asserts the exact full declaration text for a definition read. That text is `:::{definition} value`, `:phrase: value`, the body, and `:::`. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission]` asserts that each recorded definition starts with the fence and then `:phrase:`.

**2. Transitive inclusion, without duplicates or nontermination on cycles.**
- The bundle test and the `mod.rs` test both use `terms.unit` and `terms.value`, which reference each other. The tests terminate and supply each definition once. The `mod.rs` test asserts the exact list `["terms.unit","terms.value"]`.
- The acknowledgment test has `boundary` referencing `unit`. `unit` is supplied transitively and validated. When its text changes, validation reports a changed input for `terms.unit`. When the `boundary` definition input is removed from the record, validation reports that it expected one input and found none.
- `fn[declaration_text_reaches_the_model_redacted]` checks the transitive `terms.base` for both the definition read and the requirements read.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` records the same inputs twice and asserts that the recorded length stays at 2, so there are no duplicates.

**3. A term dependency introduced by an additional source read must be supplied and recorded before a submission is accepted.**
- The `mod.rs` test reads `fn[work]`, which references `terms.value`.
  - The first request does not contain "A unit of".
  - The second request, which comes before submission, does contain it.
  - The evidence inputs hold the transitive set once each.
- `fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` covers item reads and line-range reads, and checks both the supplied definitions and the recorded inputs.
- `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs]` covers paged reads. A page's definitions are delivered and recorded with its own inputs, and the term appears only on the page that uses it.

**Possible gap, judged minor.** No test has a term referenced only by a cited requirement's text rather than by the subject, a test source or an acknowledgment. A cited requirement is the same kind of declaration text as the subject. I judged this a variation within a class that is already covered, not a distinct required behavior.

I found no unasserted obligation and no acknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject, any contributed source, or an acknowledgment supplied
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
A file selected as a mandatory input MUST be visible under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`. A denied selection MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
:::{req} fixme_inputs
For a requirement or example assessment, the initial request MUST include every
valid named `{fixme}` reference to the subject found under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except a reference inside one of
the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, in this
form:
```text
Acknowledgment {
file: String,
item: String,
body: String,
issues: Array<{ reference: String, state: "open" | "closed" }>,
`file` and `item` MUST locate the containing source by project-relative path and
outline selector, using `<root>` for a whole file. `body` MUST contain the
reference's complete fenced commentary without its fences or source-comment
delimiters, including its option lines, redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. `issues` MUST give every distinct issue
its `:github:` lines name, in their order, with state supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`. Acknowledgments MUST be ordered by
file and position in the file and MUST carry no line numbers or containing
implementation source.
The locations and bodies MUST be protected against staleness by the reference-set
digest under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`; the acknowledgment MUST NOT
create an outline input merely to cover its containing source. Actual reads of
that source MUST still be recorded under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. Sources MUST satisfy
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; an inaccessible acknowledgment
MUST be reported before inference.
Terminology definitions referenced by an acknowledgment's body MUST contribute
their complete, transitive declarations to the mandatory input set under
{cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` and MUST be recorded as
definition inputs. Only the acknowledgment's body MUST contribute these
dependencies; its containing implementation source MUST NOT be supplied merely
to discover them.
